No verified study found that tests the exact gated SASRec–mean/exponential-pooling combination with all requested controls. Closest gating precedent: [HGN, Ma et al., KDD 2019](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.09217), comparing against SASRec on Amazon Books/CDs. Its formulas are Sᶠ=S⊙σ(W₁S+W₂u+b), Sⁱ=Sᶠ⊙σ(w₃ᵀSᶠ+uᵀW₄), followed by mean/max pooling. This gates embeddings rather than mixing self-attention with pooling. Amazon Books ablations: feature-gating+mean Recall@10=0.0361; both gates+mean=0.0391; both gates+max=0.0355; full HGN=0.0429. These support inexpensive aggregation, but do not isolate ungated uniform pooling.

The original [SASRec study](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.09781) supplies a last-item control: zero attention blocks. NDCG@10 falls from 0.3142 to 0.2620 on Beauty and 0.5360 to 0.4745 on Games. Attention concentrates on recent interactions in sparse datasets; residual connections carrying last-item information matter. This supports testing recency, but does not establish that learned attention beats matched fixed-decay pooling.

[Harte et al., RecSys 2023](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.09261v1) explicitly compare mean, linear/exponential decay, and last-item aggregation in LLMSeqSim alongside SASRec. Last-item aggregation performs best on sparse Amazon Beauty; however, pretrained semantic embeddings make this evidence indirect for the permitted ID-only setting. Proposed controls, not attributed paper formulas: m=Σeᵢ/L; r=Σexp[−λ(L−i)]eᵢ/Σexp[−λ(L−i)]; z=g⊙h_SASRec+(1−g)⊙r. Give mean-only, decay-only, last-item, fixed-mixture, and learned-gate variants comparable tuning priority; existing evidence does not establish the gate’s advantage.
